task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: measuring offensive reorganization independently from scoring outcomes
predicting PPP change from a structural reorganization metric
confounding by opponent and game context in absence spells
sample size and statistical power with 148 spells
measurement error in play-level derived possessions and PPP

historical_evidence.finding: Live trigger timing (early vs late detection) gave Spearman rho=-0.2066 p=1e-06 n=557 for tier vs ROG PPP, early BEST-AVOID gap 0.701 vs late 0.415. Evidence that earlier suppression triggers yield better BEST-counter outcomes, but results mixed across studies ([prior work], [prior work], [prior work]).

V1 confirmed: real player absences move the association structure (16/23 above p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; mean difference +0.142 CI[+0.103,+0.187]). V2 (LOO simulation predicts magnitude of change) failed: Spearman +0.288 p=0.077, partial +0.253 p=0.115, not confirmed.
Player routing V4 vs V5 direct scoring comparison had 8 divergences, 0 scoreable (player missing from Neo4j), hit rate n/a. Unanswerable with the data or design.

Routing prior vs H2H posterior gate diagnostic showed mean PPP delta lead-default +1.259 (n>=5) dropping to +1.129 (n>=15); low-n leaders are role players with 2-3 PPP on 5-7 possessions, inflated by small-sample distortion.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using leave-one-out simulation to predict the magnitude of structure change under absence
failed_approaches.why: Untestable due to small sample ([prior work]); Spearman correlations not significant (p=0.077, p=0.115).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing PPP for routing leaders using low-n thresholds (n>=5)
failed_approaches.why: Artifact from small-sample inflation; PPP means heavily distorted by role players with very few possessions.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing player routing versions V4 and V5 on observed PPP
failed_approaches.why: Unanswerable with available data; 0 of 8 divergences scoreable due to missing player in database and small sample.

evidence_establishes: Real player absences cause a measurable shift in the offensive association structure ([prior work] V1 confirmed).
Small possession counts dramatically inflate per-possession scoring differentials ([prior work]), which applies to any PPP change metric derived from short absence spells.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the degree of offensive reorganization predicts the resulting change in points per possession. [prior work] V2 attempted a related prediction but failed, leaving the direct correlation question open.
own_inferences: Offensive reorganization can be quantified as the distance between pre-absence and post-absence distributions of play-type frequencies, usage shares, or shot locations, using only structural descriptors that do not incorporate points scored.
The 148 spells provide adequate power for a Spearman rho of about 0.23 at 80% power (two-tailed alpha=0.05); smaller effect sizes will be undetectable.
Confounding by opponent strength, home/away, and simultaneous injuries is likely and must be controlled in a partial correlation or regression framework.

If the reorganization metric uses post-absence data that contains implicit scoring information (e.g., efficiency-weighted play selection) it will produce a mechanical correlation with PPP change rather than a true predictive relationship.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'L' (the pre-absence baseline lineup) and the temporal window for measuring reorganization are not specified and will strongly influence the result.
The reliability and stability of the reorganization metric across small possession samples (some spells may have very few possessions) is unknown.
Whether the effect size is large enough to be detected with 148 spells given realistic noise.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical evidence did not answer the question, but it exposed the small-sample limitation and the risk of artifact from low-possession comparisons. This reinforces the need for a careful power analysis and a metric isolated from scoring, but does not change the go/no-go decision.

blocking_constraints.text: 148 spells limits sensitivity to small correlations; MDE for Spearman rho is around 0.23, so a genuinely small reorganization–efficiency relationship may go undetected.
The reorganization metric must be defined a priori; if it is derived from noisy play-type counts in short spells it will have low reliability, attenuating the correlation.

prior_work.summary: [prior work] confirmed that absences change offensive structure but failed to predict the magnitude of the change. [prior work] warned that small-sample PPP differences are inflated. Neither directly tested whether the extent of reorganization predicts PPP change.

risks.text: 148 spells yields only moderate power for typical effect sizes; the study must pre-specify a minimum detectable effect and interpret null results accordingly.
Reorganization metric derived from play-type frequencies in short absence windows may have low signal-to-noise; reliability should be assessed via split-half or similar.
Opponent defensive quality, home/away, score margin, and concurrent injuries all influence both the need to reorganize and PPP change; failure to control them could produce spurious correlations.
If the reorganization metric is informed by play outcomes (e.g., efficiency of certain sets) rather than pure structural choices, it will be mechanically correlated with the PPP change outcome.
Selecting spells where the pre-absence PPP was unusually high or low can induce regression-to-the-mean that confuses the reorganization signal.
Defining L precisely is critical; shifting the baseline lineup or the pre/post window definition can alter the reorganization metric and the resulting correlation.

design.estimand: Spearman rank correlation between an a priori defined offensive reorganization index (distance from pre-absence lineup L in play-type/usage vector, computed only from structural descriptors, not points) and the change in points per possession (post-absence minus pre-absence), measured per player-absence spell.
design.unit: Player-absence spell (a contiguous set of games missed by a single player, with a consistent pre-absence lineup L and a subsequent post-absence period of at least 5 possessions).
design.sample: All qualifying spells from NBA seasons 2022-23 through 2025-26 (n ≈ 148 spells as recorded; expand if additional spells meet criteria). Use only spells with at least 10 post-absence possessions to limit noise.
design.power: With n=148, two-tailed alpha=0.05, the minimum detectable Spearman rho is approximately 0.23 at 80% power. The study is powered to detect medium-sized associations; smaller effects will be reported with confidence intervals.
design.controls: Partial Spearman correlation controlling for: (a) pre-absence PPP of the same lineup, (b) average defensive rating of opponents during the spell, (c) indicator for home/away game share, (d) presence of other rotation injuries. Sensitivity checks with additional game-state variables.
design.falsification: Placebo test: apply the same reorganization metric to contiguous non-absence games for the same team and check that the correlation with PPP change is near zero. Random permutation of spell labels among absence events.
design.multiplicity: One primary reorganization metric is pre-registered; exploratory analyses with alternative distance measures (cosine similarity, entropy difference) are reported with Bonferroni-Holm correction and labeled as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null hypothesis of no association if the partial Spearman rank correlation has a two-tailed p < 0.05. If the confidence interval for rho crosses zero despite p < 0.05, the result is treated as inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA per-game play-by-play and derived play-type possession records from the Neo4j graph database for the 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs, frozen at the analysis date.
